Definition: from G58; properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase; specially, to redeem:--buy, redeem.
BiblicalUsage: Agorazo is to buy — to go to market and purchase — and in the New Testament it becomes the great word for redemption. A man sells all to buy the field with the treasure; Paul says we were bought with a price and must glorify God in our bodies, and again, bought with a price, be not the servants of men; and heaven sings that the Lamb redeemed us to God by His blood. The word starts in the market and ends at the cross, where the price was paid in full.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this one verb holds the whole gospel. I was bought — not with silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ — and being bought means I belong to the One who paid. That is why my body and my life are not my own.
